turns.user: how do I do a deadlift
turns.reply:
Here is how to set up a solid conventional deadlift:

1. Stand feet hip-width apart, bar over mid-foot (about an inch from shins).
2. Bend at hips to grip just outside legs, keeping arms straight and shins touching the bar.
3. Wedge hips down, chest up, and pull straight up against your legs to stand tall.

This setup keeps the bar close to your center of gravity, which protects your lower back and lets you lift the most weight safely! 🏋️

turns.reply:
Here is the complete setup breakdown for a clean, strong conventional deadlift:

1. Foot Position — Feet hip-width apart, toes turned slightly out, bar directly over mid-foot.
2. Grip & Hip Hinge — Hinge down at the hips without moving the bar, gripping just outside your shins.
3. Setting the Spine — Pull your chest up, pull the slack out of the bar, and squeeze your armpits down toward your hips.
4. The Drive — Push the floor away with your legs to start the pull, keeping the bar touching your shins and thighs all the way up.
5. Lockout — Stand tall by squeezing your glutes at the top without leaning back at the lower back.
6. The Return — Hinge at the hips first to lower the bar past your knees before bending your legs to touch the floor.
